subject.title: [Bug]: Session write-lock held beyond run lifetime when agent run fails during tool execution

question: Which session-lock recovery path should own the alive same-process retained-lock failure before this issue can close?
rationale: The defect is credible, but choosing force-release, retained-use timeout, broader maxHold reclaim, or consolidation with an older lock policy issue affects session-state safety and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Require alive-holder cleanup
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100870 or a consolidated equivalent that actually releases or reclaims the retained same-process lock for this failure.

options.title: Treat dead-PID work as separate
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100878 scoped to dead-PID hardening and do not let it close this issue unless it proves the alive-holder path is covered.

options.title: Fold into broader lock policy
options.body: Route this issue into the broader live-holder/maxHold session-lock contract discussion if maintainers want one canonical reclaim policy across https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87483 and related reports.

recommendation.title: Require alive-holder cleanup
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100870 or a consolidated equivalent that actually releases or reclaims the retained same-process lock for this failure.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across session-lock policy, hold-budget, and retained-lock lifecycle code.
